own.stance_summary: USD pairs hide the real AU-versus-CA discrepancy. AUDCAD spot is at a 1y high / 5y extreme while the CA-AU 2Y yield gap that supposedly pays you to own AUD versus CAD is only median. Australian housing is transmitting tighter RBA policy after the print, and Canada still has activity, consumer, and energy-pass-through support. Short AUDCAD is the clean non-USD expression; sitting flat still pays 5% ACT/365 on the full $100m.
own.structure: spot FX short AUDCAD (sell AUD, buy CAD)
own.mispricing: AUDCAD spot is at a 1-year high and a 5-year extreme (z_5y 2.76) while CA-AU 2Y, the very differential the carry screen uses to prefer long AUD versus CAD, sits at the 51st percentile. The FX cross has overshot an ordinary rates gap. AUDUSD and USDCAD do not show that stretch because USD policy is in both prices.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: AUDCAD is a 5y extreme while the CA-AU 2Y gap is only median, so the clean AU-versus-CA view is short the cross rather than any USD pair.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Australian housing/financial-conditions evidence keeps transmitting RBA tightening while BoC energy pass-through prevents CAD from being the funding currency the spot extreme implies.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: AU housing and labor stabilize or reaccelerate, CA activity/labor deteriorate and energy risk fades, and AUDCAD holds or extends the 18 Sep high on that information.

direct_conflicts.description: catalyst-junkie, cross-merchant, perma-bull, positioning-cynic, rate-hawk, value-guy expect CAD higher while trend-follower expect CAD lower

opposing_originals.stance_summary: Valuation stretch without a dated transmission can stay wrong through the 5% ACT/365 full-$100m vig; the live discrepancy is Canada 2Y 140bp cheap versus the US after an already-priced Fed hike, with BoC energy-pass-through minutes and still-firm Canadian activity as the identifiable repricing path. Express it in CA-US_2Y rates RV, not in USDCAD, and put paper risk on at the frozen executable mark.
opposing_originals.structure: short CA-US_2Y cross-market rates RV (pay CA 2Y / receive US 2Y)
opposing_originals.mispricing: CA-US_2Y at -140.0bp is a 1y 3.77th percentile / 5y 4.31st percentile common-date gap that cheapened 15bp in five sessions into BoC minutes that were hawkish on energy, while the US leg of the gap already embeds a hike that was >90% priced. That is a fundamentals-versus-pricing gap at the 2Y tenor, not a z-score fade.
opposing_originals.horizon: 2-6 weeks through the next Canadian CPI print and BoC communication window; those calendar dates are unknown in this packet

conflict_synopsis.core_view: Canada 2Y is 140bp cheap versus a pre-priced Fed hike and should reprice higher as BoC energy-pass-through risk meets still-firm Canadian activity.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: BoC energy-pass-through minutes plus the next Canadian CPI/BoC communication versus an already-delivered Fed hike.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: CA-US_2Y breaking more negative than -140bp while oil tails fade and BoC looks through energy into weaker labor.

opposing_originals.stance_summary: Pessimism is over-discounted in the Canada versus US front-end: Canada has the strongest activity and consumer gauges in the packet while CA-US 2Y sits at a one-year extreme cheap, even as risk assets (tight HY, compressed VIX, copper at a 99th percentile) show the growth regime adapting rather than breaking. Pay Canada 2Y versus receive US 2Y to own that cyclical catch-up; the 140bp yield pickup also fights the 5% full-allocation vig, which cash does not.
opposing_originals.structure: Pay Canada 2Y versus receive US 2Y; paper instrument CA-US_2Y, side short.
opposing_originals.mispricing: Canada 2Y trades 140bp through US 2Y at a 1y 3.77th / 5y 4.31st percentile even though Canada has the strongest activity and consumer gauges and the BoC has flagged energy pass-through. The closing mechanism is Canada yields rising relative to the US (BoC forced to respect growth plus energy) and/or the US front end, already at a 1y extreme after a delivered hike, failing to cheapen as much as the 140bp Canada discount implies.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: Canada cyclical strength and energy-inflation risk are underpriced versus the US in the 2Y, where CA-US sits at a 1y extreme of -140bps; pay CA versus receive US.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Canada data and BoC energy pass-through force CA 2Y to re-rate higher versus an already-hawkish US front end.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: Canada activity/consumer lose their lead, or CA-US_2Y makes a new 1y low as labor weakness keeps BoC easy and US yields cheapen Canada further.

opposing_originals.stance_summary: Post-FOMC long-10Y / bull-flatten is already owned in price and holdings; CAD and JPY FX crowding has either covered or already jumped, so the cleaner fade is a US 2s10s steepener against asset-manager 10Y length rather than joining duration longs or chasing spot.
opposing_originals.structure: Outright short US 2s10s curve (paper steepener: short 10s vs long 2s in book units).
opposing_originals.mispricing: Market-vs-market and ownership-vs-price: the post-hike easing/flatten path is in the 1y extreme of US 2s10s (25.0bp, 0.198th percentile) while the holder of that view—asset-manager 10Y net length—is itself at a 3y 97th percentile. That is crowded ownership sitting on an already-completed price move, not a fresh discrepancy.
opposing_originals.horizon: 2-6 weeks, through the next US inflation/labor prints that can force AM 10Y length to reassess the easing-path flatten.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: Fade the already-owned post-hike bull-flatten/long-10Y complex with a US 2s10s steepener; do not join duration longs or chase CAD/JPY FX after covering and a 1d USDJPY jump.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Next US inflation/labor print that forces crowded AM 10Y flattening longs to reassess the post-hike easing path.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: Bull-flatten remains pinned at the 1y extreme while AM 10Y net length stays historically elevated, or data re-open an easing path those longs own.

opposing_originals.stance_summary: Canada’s front end has not priced the same higher-for-longer impulse the Fed just delivered: CA-US 2Y sits at -140bp near the cheap tail of both 1y and 5y distributions while BoC energy pass-through risk, 3% headline CPI, and above-50 Canadian activity/consumer scores argue against the priced BoC-Fed divergence. Short the CA-US 2Y spread; do not chase already 99th-percentile Australian yields.
opposing_originals.structure: Short CA-US 2Y government-yield spread (short CA 2Y duration versus long US 2Y duration)
opposing_originals.mispricing: CA-US 2Y at -140.0 bps is in the bottom ~4th percentile of both 1y and 5y history (z_1y -1.84, z_5y -1.51) after a further -17bp 1m widening. That spread prices a BoC path far easier than a Fed that just hiked with core PCE still ~3% 6m annualized. Canadian headline CPI still 3.0%, GDP +0.8% q/q, and BoC minutes on energy pass-through are not consistent with that gap. The mispricing is the cross-market 2Y differential, not the absolute US 2Y level (already 99.8th percentile 1y after a pre-priced hike).
opposing_originals.horizon: 2-8 weeks through the next Canadian CPI composition prints and BoC communication after the energy-pass-through warning

conflict_synopsis.core_view: Canadian 2Y has not priced the Fed’s delivered hike and BoC energy/activity facts, so CA-US 2Y at -140bp should reprice higher.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Canadian CPI composition and BoC follow-through on the energy-pass-through warning after a Fed hike that was already priced.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: CA-US 2Y cheapens further on a US-only selloff, or Canadian core/labor confirm the BoC can ignore energy and keep diverging easier.

opposing_originals.stance_summary: Canada 5Y versus US 5Y is a dual-horizon historical tail, not a dip. The valuation anchor is the frozen CA-US 5Y spread at the 0.20th 1y / 6.95th 5y percentile after a 16bp 1m cheapening into a Fed hike that was already >90% priced. Convergence belongs in rates RV: short CA-US_5Y (Canada yields up versus US / US yields down versus Canada). Spot USDCAD is only moderately rich and is the inferior expression of the same relative gap.
opposing_originals.structure: Short the frozen CA-US 5Y sovereign yield spread (CA 5Y minus US 5Y). Book engine marks CA-US_5Y from market_state.rate_rv.CA-US_5Y.bps. Economically long US 5Y versus short Canada 5Y.
opposing_originals.mispricing: Valuation anchor is the CA-US 5Y spread versus its own 1y and 5y distributions, not the 1m yield change. At -124bp the spread is a 0.20th percentile 1y / 6.95th percentile 5y reading (z_1y -2.03) after a further 16bp 1m cheapening. That is historically too much Canada-versus-US cheapness once the priced Fed hike is stripped out. Peer check: CA-US_2Y is also a 4th-percentile 5y tail; USDCAD is not.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: CA-US 5Y at -124bp is a 0.20th 1y / 6.95th 5y historical tail after a priced Fed hike, so Canada-versus-US cheapness should converge in rates RV rather than in only-moderately-rich USDCAD.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: The 16 Sep 2026 Fed hike was already >90% priced; remaining 1y-tail CA-US 5Y cheapness should start converging as that event premium fades and/or BoC energy pass-through re-rates Canada.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: CA-US_5Y holds or extends the 0.20th 1y tail because Canada core and labor stay clearly softer than the US, not because of short timing noise.

opposing_originals.stance_summary: US front-end yields, the Sep 16 hike and August CPI tightening bias are still aligned. Short US 2Y duration is the cleanest continuation; fading 99th-percentile yields or the 1-day Canada dip is premature. USDCAD is the spot alternative but is a weaker, 1-month-only trend versus an unambiguous 1d/5d/1m/3m US 2Y backup. Flat $100m still pays 5% ACT/365, so this empty book must own the live trend.
opposing_originals.structure: outright short US 2Y duration (pay fixed); paper mark is the 2Y yield
opposing_originals.mispricing: The live gap is not 'yields are high so buy duration.' It is the assumption that a fully priced hike plus 1y z of 2.84 is sufficient to fade a still-rising 2Y. Market-implied into 16 Sep required the 25bp hike; it did not require the subsequent 2Y backup or a still-open tightening bias. Fading that tape is the premature reversal. USDCAD does not own the same gap: 3m USDCAD is down even as US 2Y is up on every horizon.
opposing_originals.horizon: 4-8 weeks, through the next US inflation prints and FOMC cycle

conflict_synopsis.core_view: US 2Y, the delivered hike and August CPI tightening bias remain aligned, so continue to pay the front end rather than fade 99th-percentile yields.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Post-hike US front-end follow-through while August CPI keeps the tightening bias intact.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: US 2Y 1-month uptrend reverses or US inflation/labor evidence removes the Fed tightening bias.
